381-program-description: Four fields plus methods. Enter at the start of U2. Keep a 3.3 average in POLI with over half at B+ or higher, and CGPA 3.00.
381-complementary-courses-45-credits: 12 at 200, 3 in each of the four fields; 33 at 300+. 6 of Methods at 300–400 (the 9 with POLI 210 must be at McGill). At least 12 at 400+, including a 500-level Honours Seminar at McGill.
At most 24 in one field (27 for Comparative). Upper-level courses need a 200-level one in that field. At most 15 transfer.
383-program-description: Four fields plus methods, with another Arts discipline. Enter in U1. Keep a 3.3 average with over half at B+, CGPA 3.00, and the other department's rules.
383-complementary-courses-33-credits: 3 of Methods at 300–400 (the 6 with POLI 210 at McGill). 9 at 200, at most 3 per field; 24 at 300+. At least 9 at 400+, including a 500-level Honours Seminar at McGill. At most 18 in one field (21 for Comparative) and 12 transfer.
386-population-and-global-health: An action-oriented program on public health challenges, grounded in equity, justice and allyship, with community research and policy work.
You learn to evaluate health inequities, analyze health systems, design ethical and sustainable policy, and apply this in practicum and field settings.
386-experiential-learning-and-partnershi: Applied research, policy labs and community projects, with practicums in equity, sustainability, planetary health, reproductive health, prevention, Indigenous and immigrant health, policy and community health.
386-careers-and-further-study: Policy, research, advocacy and public service, or graduate programs in public health, law, social sciences, health administration, medicine and global development.
386-research-and-teaching-environment: Faculty from public health, policy, sociology, anthropology, geography, Indigenous and critical race studies, environment, ethics and law.
386-faculty-program-in-population-and-gl: Tools to understand and address what shapes health locally and globally, open to diverse backgrounds. Themes: determinants, equity, planetary health, decolonizing and anti-racist approaches, policy, and community research.
Includes a field practicum in your third and final year with agencies, NGOs, academic centres or community groups.
386-admission-requirements-bachelor-of-a: You must meet all Faculty and program requirements (p. 151).
386-bachelor-of-arts-in-population-and-g: Welcomes wide backgrounds, including lived experience and non-traditional paths; no set academic background, but interest in interdisciplinary and systems thinking.
Also needs a list of non-academic activities and three short essays of 250–300 words. Meeting these doesn't guarantee admission. Taught in English, but some Québec placements need working French.
387-application-procedures: Upload everything to McGill's admissions system by the deadline.
387-application-dates-and-deadlines: Enrolment Services sets opening dates. Check the Department's site and whether your program has its own deadline.
387-location: School: 2001 McGill College, Suite 1200. Department: Room 1253. Student Affairs Officer: Enoch Leung.
387-program-description: Competency-based, on health equity, population, global and Indigenous health, ethics, data literacy, research methods and knowledge translation. Team-based, community-engaged learning, with some blended courses.
Streams: Environment and Health; Culture, Society and Health; Diet, Lifestyle and the Life Course; Systems, Policy and Government; Innovation and Leadership.
387-complementary-courses-21-credits: From one stream: at most 9 at 200, at least 12 at 300+. Others with the adviser's permission.
388-stream-1-environment-and-health: Some courses have prerequisites or limited seats.
389-stream-5-innovation-and-leadership: ECON 230D1 and D2 together if chosen. Desautels courses are capped with no priority, so allow at least four terms.
391-about-psychology: Programs in Arts and Science; Science's are for science students only. See p. 1274. These degrees are academic, not a professional qualification in psychology.
391-information-meetings-for-new-student: Attend before registering: June for CEGEP entrants, August for others; B.Sc. students have a separate one. Bring transcripts and look at this catalogue and the schedule first. January entrants should see an adviser in early December.
391-program-description: Only for Arts Psychology majors, for a more specialized degree.
391-program-requirements: Makes room for courses needed for graduate school and the Ordre des Psychologues' undergraduate credits. It counts as a second minor, so you also need one outside Psychology (Educational Psychology doesn't qualify).
391-complementary-courses-18-credits: 3 from List A, 3 from List B, 3 at 400–500, and 9 at 300+ in PSYC, ANTH, LING or SOCI.
391-list-a-behavioural-neuroscience-cogn: With COMP 202 or 204, linear algebra and calculus, consider COMP 551. Psychology and CS students are encouraged to take COMP 551 over PSYC 560.
392-unclassified-courses: Research and topics courses can count too.
393-program-description: A focused introduction to specialized topics, complementing your main field.
393-program-requirements: For B.A. students in other departments. Expandable to the Major.
393-program-prerequisites-03-credits: Introductory psychology in CEGEP, or PSYC 100 in first year.
393-program-description-2: An overview of core areas and advanced topics, with optional research. It may not be enough for some graduate programs; add the Behavioural Science minor for those or the Ordre's credits.
393-program-prerequisites-06-credits: Introductory psychology and biology from CEGEP, or PSYC 100 and BIOL 115, 111 or 112 in first year.
394-u1-or-u2: For Honours, finish required courses including PSYC 305 in U1, and 27 graded credits in the year before applying.

Exempt from PSYC 204 with 75%+ in Quantitative Methods plus Advanced Quantitative Methods or Statistics for Social Science, or in Probability and Statistics. Replace with 3 credits at 300+ in PSYC, ANTH, LING or SOCI.
395-program-description: An in-depth overview with a required two-term research course and seminar, emphasizing research techniques and statistics, with room for graduate school and Ordre requirements. Selective admission.
395-program-requirements: Apply usually at the end of U1, or U2 with fewer seats. Needs 27 graded credits the year before, PSYC 204, 211, 212, 213, 215 and 305, and CGPA 3.50; the typical cut-off is about 3.75. GPA 3.00 in U2 to continue.
Decisions come by email before classes in September.
Honours: CGPA 3.00 and B in PSYC 380D and 306. First Class: CGPA 3.50 and A- in both.
396-program-prerequisites-06-credits: Introductory psychology, biology and statistics from CEGEP, or first-year equivalents.
396-u1: Same PSYC 204 exemptions, replaced with 3 credits at 300 in PSYC, ANTH, LING or SOCI.
396-u1-or-u2: PSYC 305 in U1 and 27 graded credits the year before applying.
397-complementary-courses-27-credits: 3–9 from 500-level PSYC or the list; the rest of 9 from 400-level. Earlier PSYC 385, 484D or 485 can count for those entering in U3. Then 18 Honours credits.
397-list-b-social-health-and-development: 6 from the list, and 6 at 300+ in ANTH, LING, PSYC or SOCI.
398-program-description: Core areas with a two-term research course. Not as complete as Honours, so may not cover some graduate programs or the Ordre's credits. Selective.
398-program-requirements: Combine with another Arts discipline, with an adviser in each. Same entry as Honours: 27 graded credits, the six PSYC courses, CGPA 3.50 (typically about 3.75), and GPA 3.00 in U2.
Joint Honours: CGPA 3.00, B in PSYC 380D and 306. First Class: 3.50 and A-.
399-program-prerequisites-06-credits: Introductory psychology, biology and statistics from CEGEP, or first-year equivalents.
